newsitem.title: USA: Phillips, Seaway plan oil pipeline expansion.
newsitem.headline: Phillips, Seaway plan oil pipeline expansion.

text.p: Phillips Pipe Line Co, a subsidiary of Phillips Petroleum Co, said Monday it signed a letter of intent with Seaway Pipeline Co to expand and build new oil product lines to U.S. Midwest markets.

Phillips said the parent company's board of directors approved participation in a plan to not only expand and convert a portion of the Seaway system, but also to build a new pipeline from Cushing, Oklahoma to Wichita, Kansas.
The new system will be common carrier and transport gasoline and distillates to markets in the Midwest.

"The project is part of Phillips Pipe Line's strategy to expand its transportation network in the Midwest, where the company already has a strong presence and where demand for refined products transportation continues to increase," said PPL President Tom Rich.

Included in the project is a plan to expand and convert Seaway's 20-inch crude oil pipeline, which currently extends from Galena Park, Texas, to Cushing. A five-mile extension is to be built from Phillips' Pasadena, Texas, terminal to Galena Park.
The pipeline will be converted to transport oil products.
In addition, the plan calls for the connection of the Seaway pipeline to a new 18-inch, 150-mile pipeline that PPL is to build from Cushing to Wichita.
Construction was seen starting in the first quarter of 1997 and completed by first quarter 1998.
Cost was not disclosed, and the project was subject to negotiation of definition agreements, and to approval by PPL's board of directors and Seaway partners.
Seaway is a partnership of subsidiaries of Phillips and ARCO.
Seaway also operates a 30-inch crude pipeline from Freeport, Texas to Cushing.
